title: Haloumi Madras-Style Curry
subtitle: with Crispy Flatbreads
description: Whether you're full-time vego or part-time only, our varied range of vegetarian dishes really hits the spot. Bursting with veggies, dairy, legumes, grains and nuts, they're packed with flavour, they’ll fill you up and they're totally mouth-watering too!

steps.text: Prep ingredients: Preheat the oven to 220C, fan-forced, for the tortillas (see Make it yours). Line an oven tray with baking paper. Thinly slice the onion. Finely chop the tomato. Cut the zucchini into 2cm chunks. Crush or finely chop 2 garlic cloves. Cut the haloumi into 3cm chunks.

Fry haloumi: Heat 2 tsp olive oil in a medium deep frypan over medium-high heat. Cook the haloumi, turning, for 2-3 mins until golden. Remove from the pan. Heat 2 tsp olive oil in the pan over medium heat and cook the onion, stirring, for 3-4 mins until softened. Add the curry powder and cook, stirring, for 1 min or until fragrant.

Cook curry: Stir the tomato, tomato paste and 250ml (1 cup) water into the onion mixture and bring to the boil. Reduce heat to medium-high, add the zucchini and cook for 5 mins or until tender. Add the haloumi, 20g butter and 2 tsp sugar and cook, stirring, for 2-3 mins until the sugar is dissolved. Remove the pan from the heat. Taste, then season with salt and pepper.

Bake flatbreads: Meanwhile, combine the garlic and 1 tbs olive oil in a bowl and season with salt and pepper. Brush the tortillas with the garlic oil and put on the lined tray. Bake, turning over halfway, for 6-8 mins until crisp and golden.
Serve up: Stir the yoghurt into the curry. Divide the haloumi curry among bowls and serve with the flatbreads. Enjoy!

Make it yours: If you don't want to use the oven to bake the tortillas, try pan-frying them – it takes a bit longer, but gives them a deliciously crispy edge! Brush the tortillas with the garlic oil, then pan-fry them, in batches, transferring to a plate and covering with foil to keep warm.
